intake: believer — practicing Roman Catholic (weekly Mass, daily office, confession a few times a year), returned to it as an adult rather than merely inheriting it; holds classical theism roughly as Aquinas states it, and as a data analyst does not think an RCT is the kind of instrument that could bear on it either way.

walk.note: Fair as biography of how I came in, thin as an account of what religion is, but the move itself carries me.
I take it for my own reasons: the Church teaches God can be known from the world by natural reason, but Aquinas never left Religion behind to get here; this is a supplement, not a replacement.

Classical theism does not deny that God has intellect and will; 'a God who chooses' is Aquinas's position, not its refutation, and being itself was never supposed to show up as one datum among others.

'Outcomes should line up with prayer' is a prediction no serious theology makes; STEP tested a lever model of prayer that nobody in the tradition holds, and primary causation through secondary causes is not 'hiding by design', it is just not an extra force.
'Does not seem to reduce' gives you non-reduction, not two kinds of substance; hylomorphism, property dualism and neutral monism are all sitting between the premise and Descartes.
Elisabeth's question is a real objection to Descartes, and dependence of every mental function on the brain is granted, but dependence is not identity; the author concedes the gap herself at move 8.

I agree physics describes structure and not what has it, but that gap can be filled by Russellian monism or by being itself; 'reality is at bottom mind' is one option among several, and the one I would reach for is the one set down at move 3.
A dream needs a dreamer; I take that, though I would not have set aside the larger candidate dreamer at moves 3 and 4.
'The problem begins with I, and then necessarily You' is Buber as much as Strawson, and I take it gladly; I notice I am moved by the sentence and have checked that the argument holds without it.
I would choose mercy too, though for me it is commanded (the neighbour as the hidden Christ) rather than chosen under uncertainty; the move still carries me.
Docta ignorantia is where I actually live, though Cusa reached it through theology, not by leaving it.

Hope held knowingly, fidelity in the present toward what is unseen: this is Hebrews 11 and I take it; but I hope because of a promise, not because hoping 'generally leads to increased goodness', and the non-fungibility of each subject is something my tradition has always said.
Pure act, non-discursive knowing, nothing forgotten: that is Aquinas and I land here; but 'resolved' smuggles in 'closed', which actus purus does not mean.
'More of a bargain than an argument' tells me nothing about what the bargain is or between whom, and the object has silently changed from a maker to a 'benevolent future system'.

'To think is to ignore' is true of minds that attend by selecting, which is every mind we have met; the author's own caveat admits it has not been shown to hold for a mind that is the act of being rather than a process in time.
Granting no maker, suffering is still bad for the sufferer; Aquinas also locates the good in beings as their perfection, so I take the move and leave the grounding question where the critics left it.

That each being's continuity matters and that the self is not the same as its carrier is near enough to resurrection hope that I take it; what strikes me is that the carrier this position needs, a conscious other who forgets nothing, is the mind discarded at move 16.

I would not wait for data from a machine to learn whether a self can be carried; the question the route pauses on has an older answer it set down two moves back, and I would stand at the edge facing the other way.

first_exit.why: The dilemma at move 3 refutes a position Aquinas did not hold: classical theism says God has intellect and will, so a God who chooses not to be seen is the view, not a contradiction of it. And the demand that being itself appear as one datum among the data is a category mistake about what the position claims, the same mistake the author later catches Ryle naming.

comment: The gap you name at move 8 (physics describes structure but not what has it) and the carrier you need at move 18 (a conscious other who forgets nothing and holds a self apart from what it is made of) are both shaped exactly like the God you set down at move 3, and you set that God down on a reading of classical theism that Aquinas would not recognise, since he never denied that God wills. Your second half is the most honest account of hope I have read from someone outside the Church, and I distrust how much that moved me, so I checked: the premise doing the work at move 16 is one your own caveat admits is unproven. If to think is not necessarily to ignore, the route does not pause at Materialism₂; it closes at Classical theism₂, and the mercy you chose at move 11 has a face.
